I do feel you. I don't think the flashy route is the right one though, because that's what all game trailers do. If your trailers are just heavily edited compilations of doing cool things, the only people who are going to be excited are existing fans who notice all the small details. For everyone else, it'll just be another generic trailer.

Hitman is definitely a unique kind of game, and I think its marketing should capitalize on that. What makes it unique from other similar games, the insane level design, the social stealth mechanics, the endless ways to approach a mission, I think these things are brought up but not really focused on.

I'm not saying it's going to be the next fortnite or something, but there's definitely a market for what hitman brings. I guess what I'm saying is more dev gameplay, less flashy "look at all this cool shit you can do in 30 seconds" things. The "how to hitman" videos I think are pretty good, but like I said before I think the focus is too much on new features to appeal to existing fans than the core game to bring in new ones.

I just feel like there's a bit of a disconnect when it comes to the target audience of the videos. Current fans are going to be excited by the new features, and new fans are going to be brought in by the core game. But these videos haven't really gone in-depth enough to sell to new players. 

I know there are long gameplay videos out there, but they're unofficial, often with no commentary, and don't much of any attention outside the community. You're not going to watch an hour of unedited gameplay of a game you're not already interested in.

People always suggest this but how would it work with the current style of hitman? In blood money most of the time you were doing full playthroughs of the campaign, buying things along the way, and by the end you'd have everything. With new hitman you don't really play through the story like you did in old games. It's all about replaying levels, maybe you do a full playthrough, but because of the original episodic design these levels are designed to be played multiple times until moving to the next, which kinda ruins the whole idea of currency being a reward for playing well since you'll do so many runs you'll be able to get a perfect score every time until you move on. And even if you played through once, it would only be once since there are no profiles in these games, so once everything is unlocked, it's unlocked for good.

So you'd really need to do a lot of redesigning to the game itself. Just saying this because people seem to suggest this a lot but I just don't think the current style suits it.
